Image/Data Credits

The people and sources behind our state adventures. Data is bundled with the game for offline play; these links need a connection.

◀ Back to QuizTrekker - US States

Population and largest communities

U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program, Vintage 2025: resident population as of July 1, 2025, from NST-EST2025-ALLDATA.csv, field POPESTIMATE2025, state records only. Rank 1 is the most populous of the 50 states; DC and territories are excluded. These are estimates, not live counts or a new decennial census.

Vintage 2025 cities and towns estimates, sub-est2025.csv: ten largest incorporated places per state (SUMLEV 162), using official Census names. Lists include cities, boroughs, villages and legal consolidated-city balances. A name containing “metropolitan government” describes the municipal government, not an MSA population. Metro-area rankings are not used.

Rhode Island exception: its eight incorporated cities cannot make a top-ten list. Its list therefore ranks cities and towns (municipal county subdivisions, SUMLEV 061) using the same July 1, 2025 estimates. This avoids duplicating the cities in two geography levels.

Hawaii exception: Hawaii has no conventional incorporated cities. Its ten largest Census-designated places (CDPs) use 2020–2024 ACS 5-year estimates, table B01003. These are period estimates from a different methodology, not July 2025 point estimates. ACS margins of error exist; lists are ordered by the published point estimates. The state population and Population Showdown still use Census July 2025 state estimates for every state.

Raw Census downloads: state CSV, places CSV, ACS B01003, ACS geography labels.

Area and Size Showdown

U.S. Census Bureau: State Area Measurements, 2010. Measurements reflect January 1, 2010 boundaries and MAF/TIGER updates through August 2010. Values are rounded square miles. Total area includes land and water; rank 1 is the largest of 50 states by total area. Land and water details are shown separately. Rounding can make their sum differ from the displayed total by one square mile. Size Showdown uses total area consistently.

Highest points

Highest natural points of the 50 U.S. states: Census Statistical Abstract 2012, Table 366, citing USGS Elevations and Distances (April 2005). Elevations are approximate published reference values; newer surveys may differ. Meters are converted from feet using 0.3048 and rounded. Alaska uses the newer NPS 20,310-foot elevation. Current names include Black Elk Peak and Kuwohi. Connecticut’s point is Mount Frissell’s south slope, not the summit. Highest-point data for optional non-state locations is not yet included.

Statehood

Congressional Research Service, R47747: Admission of States to the Union: A Historical Reference Guide, Table 1. Dates and order for the original 13 states use ratification of the U.S. Constitution; later states use effective admission dates. North and South Dakota share a date; conventional order is 39 and 40. Statehood Timeline accepts either order for states admitted on the same date. All 50 bundled records were checked against this table.

State flags

Flagpedia’s U.S. state SVG package, downloaded November 14, 2026 (package page last updated February 6, 2026), based on Wikimedia Commons vector files. Flagpedia offers these designs as public domain. The original SVGs are stored locally, mapped to state abbreviations and displayed without stretching.

Current designs checked against official sources: Minnesota (May 11, 2024), Mississippi (January 11, 2021), and Utah (March 9, 2024).

Maps and neighboring states

US Atlas 3.0.1, Michael Bostock, based on U.S. Census Bureau 2017 cartographic boundaries. ISC license. Outlines preserve the source Albers USA projection and proportions; Alaska and Hawaii are insets, with Alaska reduced. Small islands and borders reflect cartographic simplification.

The Neighboring States game counts shared land and river borders. Lake-only, ocean-only and corner-only contacts do not count. U.S. adjacency follows shared US Atlas arcs without the former Michigan–Illinois, Michigan–Minnesota or New York–Rhode Island water-only additions. Ontario–Ohio and Ontario–Pennsylvania lake-only borders are excluded; Michigan–Ontario river borders are retained. See Canada Water Agency’s Lake Erie map and Michigan’s St. Marys River boundary description. Alaska and Hawaii have no neighboring U.S. states.

Symbols, nicknames and landmarks

Factual symbol names and mottos are compiled from the reference lists of state birds, flowers, mottos, and nicknames, checked November 14, 2026. Wikipedia contributors; CC BY-SA 4.0 for adapted reference text. Common nicknames are a selected example, not every nickname; traditional or unofficial mottos are labeled. Multiple floral or bird designations are labeled where applicable.

Each state includes one selected National Park Service landmark or park, with a direct link to its official page. These are examples to explore, not a popularity ranking or an exhaustive landmark list.

Capital locations

The 50 U.S. state capital stars use WGS84 state capitol-building coordinates from the USGS National Map structures service, distributed in the public-domain Vega state capitals dataset. Snapshot: November 15, 2026; checked against the USGS service. Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program.

Points use the outline’s exact Albers USA projection: scale 1300, translation [487.5, 305], including Alaska and Hawaii insets. All 50 points fall inside their rendered state outlines. Star centers stay at these projected coordinates; labels and dotted leaders adjust for readability. Simplified outlines are educational, not survey maps.

Optional U.S. and Canadian geography

The 50 U.S. states remain the default. Independent optional packs add seven U.S. territories/D.C. entries, ten Canadian provinces, and three Canadian territories (70 locations in total). D.C. is identified as a federal district; Canadian provinces and territories are not U.S. states. Non-state entries have no statehood dates or admission order. Statehood Timeline always uses the 50 U.S. states.

Government boundaries and capital points

D.C., Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, and the U.S. Virgin Islands: U.S. Census TIGERweb State/Equivalent boundaries and area attributes, retrieved November 15, 2026. Territorial government-building points come from the USGS National Map. D.C. has no separate district capital; no capital star is invented.

Canada: Statistics Canada 2021 cartographic province/territory boundaries, reproduced and generalized under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. Small coastal features are simplified; the capital’s containing outline retains finer detail. Capital city reference points are from the authoritative Natural Resources Canada Canadian Geographical Names Database. These are official city reference points, not necessarily legislative-building coordinates.

The optional outlines use equirectangular projections (Canada at 55°N, island areas locally centered); compare-at-map-scale remains limited to the original U.S. state map. Canadian location maps show all 13 provinces/territories even when some are excluded from quizzes. U.S. island location tiles show their own outlines rather than placing them on the contiguous-U.S. map. All outlines are educational, not navigational or survey boundaries.

Minor Outlying Islands: one entry, nine insets

UM combines Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston, Kingman, Midway, Navassa, Palmyra, and Wake. All nine shoreline groups are extracted from GSHHG 2.3.7 full-resolution L1 shorelines in the NOAA NCEI archive, by Paul Wessel and Walter H. F. Smith (SOEST/NOAA). The combined display arranges the groups as independent insets, not at geographic positions or a common scale. There is no common capital and no fabricated population or area total. UM appears in Learn, Shape Challenge and neighbor rounds; numeric Showdowns exclude it.

GSHHG-derived data are distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3 or later: original notice, LGPL terms, GPL terms. The extracted coordinates and projection/inset source are available in the repository’s data and build source. Island context: NOAA, Midway FWS, Navassa FWS.

Facts, flags and comparison methods

Canadian population: 2021 Census counts published February 9, 2022 (census reference date May 11, 2021). Canadian land/freshwater areas: Statistics Canada, Canada Year Book 2011 Table 15.6, source NRCan Atlas of Canada. U.S. island-area population: 2020 Census Island Areas release; D.C. 2020 Census; Puerto Rico 2020 Census. Each expanded profile identifies its own vintage and source. Existing U.S. state ranks remain ranks among the 50 states; no mixed international rank is implied.

Population Showdowns choose pairs with the same reference date: original U.S. states use 2025 estimates, optional U.S. entries use the 2020 Census, and Canadian entries use the 2021 Census. Expanded Size Showdowns compare land area only, avoiding incompatible marine/freshwater totals; source vintages still differ and are shown in feedback. Default 50-state Size Showdowns continue to compare 2010 total area including water.

Canadian capitals, flags, birds, floral emblems and available mottos: Government of Canada, Canadian Heritage provincial/territorial symbols (individual sources linked on each profile). Flag photographs are reproduced from those official pages without changing their proportions; no endorsement is implied. U.S. territory flags and the U.S. national flag used for UM: Flagpedia/FlagCDN, locally bundled public-domain SVGs. The D.C. flag is a code-rendered version of the design described by the D.C. Office of the Secretary.

Expanded neighbor lists are curated from government boundary maps: shared land and river borders, excluding lake-only and ocean-only borders. Corner-only contacts (such as Saskatchewan/Nunavut and Manitoba/Northwest Territories) and new offshore maritime contacts are excluded. Quiz answers include only enabled locations; More Facts may also name disabled neighbors. All datasets and flags are bundled locally for offline play.

Neighbor teaching maps

U.S.-only maps use the original US Atlas Albers USA projection and Alaska/Hawaii insets. Cross-border maps invert that exact projection for U.S. boundaries, then use the same equirectangular frame at 55°N as the pinned Canadian/territorial source boundaries. No states are moved to illustrate adjacency. Shared land and river boundaries follow the documented neighbor graph. Postal-code labels and full-name keys supplement result colors. Comparison popups retain the original fact-source dates and definitions.

Game artwork and future credits

QuizTrekker - US States logo and coordinated app artwork are supplied/generated project assets. Game buttons and interface illustrations are rendered in code. New image sets and datasets will receive their own source, date, usage notes and license entries here as they are added.

Data snapshot: November 16, 2026 · QuizTrekker - US States 0.14.0. Reproducible facts and source checksums are available in the source repository.
